prompt:
Create a high-fidelity desktop web app UI composition for a new Analytics workspace in the existing ASC Studio application. Use the attached ASC Studio Overview screenshot strictly as the identity and chrome reference: preserve its exact left sidebar proportions, top bar height, light neutral canvas, white flat panels, blue accent, Inter-like typography, thin gray hairlines, compact 7–9px corner radii, restrained status colors, readable 13–17px operational text, and shadowless professional operator feel. Do not copy the Overview page's content or panel arrangement.

Viewport is a wide 1919×1088 desktop app screenshot. Keep the existing sidebar and app picker. Insert Analytics directly below Overview in the sidebar and make Analytics the active soft-blue row. Existing items TestFlight, Releases, Apple Ads, Reviews remain visible. Header: "Analytics" with subtitle "Understand what changed and where to act next." Right side has date range "Last 30 days", Compare "Previous period", Filters, and a quiet "Refresh" control. All visualized values are clearly labeled "Sample data" in a small neutral badge so no screenshot implies live facts.

Direction: WHAT CHANGED WORKBENCH. This is a question-led diagnostic surface, not a KPI-card dashboard and not a chat interface. At the top of the workspace, create a slim horizontal question switcher with four precise tabs: "What changed?", "Where did it change?", "How are users converting?", "What should I inspect?" Make "What changed?" active with blue underline/soft-blue fill. Under it, show a compact four-column performance strip: Downloads 12,480 +8.4%, Product page views 38,210 +3.1%, Conversion 32.7% +1.6 pt, Proceeds $18,420 +11.2%. Every metric has tiny source/freshness text; no overall rating.

Dominant focal moment: a wide chart titled "Downloads changed most after Aug 6" taking roughly two-thirds of the first evidence row. It overlays blue current-period and dashed gray previous-period lines, with an Aug 6 Release 1.1.4 annotation, a selected Aug 5–12 interval, and exact hover values shown in a restrained tooltip. Keep the language evidentiary: subtitle "Daily downloads rose 77.8% on Aug 6; the release occurred the same day." Add a small "Correlation, not causation" label.

To the right of the chart, create a narrow "What drove the change" ranked contribution panel with rows United States +620, Mexico +310, App Store Search +280, Product page GLP-1 Basics -94 and restrained horizontal bars. Below the first row, use a full-width "Evidence and next checks" table with columns Observation, Evidence, Confidence, Inspect. Rows:
- "Mexico conversion increased 2.4 pt" — "Views +6%, downloads +15%" — "High" — button "Open Storefront"
- "Search drove 280 additional downloads" — "Source contribution" — "High" — "Open acquisition"
- "Session decline concentrated on 1.1.4" — "Usage opt-in 24%" — "Limited" — "Open Releases"
- "Campaign spend rose without matching downloads" — "Apple Ads + Analytics" — "Medium" — "Open Apple Ads"
Use small semantic status dots, not colorful pills.

At the bottom, include a concise source strip: engagement complete through Aug 17; downloads through Aug 19; usage opt-in 24%; privacy-suppressed rows are missing, not zero. Include one modest AI action labeled "Explain selected evidence" with a plain document/chat icon, not sparkles, and a note "Uses only the selected aggregates and cites every claim." It must be secondary and never auto-generate recommendations.

No saved-view rail and no portfolio roster. Use line charts and semantic HTML-style controls, no gradients, no glass, no oversized typography, no bento-card collage, no fake AI sparkle motif, no dark theme, no 3D, no illustrations. The surface's job must read instantly as answer a concrete business question using cited, cautious evidence, then deep-link to the owning workflow. Produce only the UI screenshot, no surrounding device frame, no browser chrome, no caption outside the app.
